class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Smith-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>His maternal grandfather, <a href="/wiki/Joshua_N._Haldeman" title="Joshua N. Haldeman">Joshua N. Haldeman</a>, who died in a plane crash when Elon was a toddler, was an American-born Canadian chiropractor, aviator and political activist in the <a href="/wiki/Technocracy_movement" title="Technocracy movement">Technocracy movement</a><sup id="cite_ref-16" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-16"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>14<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:8_17-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:8-17"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>15<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> who moved to South Africa in 1950.<sup id="cite_ref-McGreal_18-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-McGreal-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Haldeman's anti-government, anti-democratic and conspiracist views, which included the promotion of far-right antisemitic conspiracy theories,<sup id="cite_ref-19" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Benton2_20-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Benton2-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> "fanatical" support of <a href="/wiki/Apartheid" title="Apartheid">apartheid</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-Benton2_20-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Benton2-20"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and according to Errol Musk, support of <a href="/wiki/Nazism" title="Nazism">Nazism</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-McGreal_18-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-McGreal-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>16<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> have been suggested as an <a href="/wiki/Joshua_N._Haldeman#Influence_on_Elon_Musk" title="Joshua N. Haldeman">influence on Elon</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-:03_21-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:03-21"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>19<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-22" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-22"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>20<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:13_23-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:13-23"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>21<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-24" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-24"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>22<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> During his childhood, Elon was told stories by his grandmother of Haldeman's travels and exploits, and Elon has suggested that all of Haldeman's descendants have his "desire for adventure, exploration – doing crazy things".<sup id="cite_ref-25" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-25"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>23<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Elon has a younger brother, <a href="/wiki/Kimbal_Musk" title="Kimbal Musk">Kimbal</a>, a younger sister, <a href="/wiki/Tosca_Musk" title="Tosca Musk">Tosca</a>, and four paternal half-siblings.<sup id="cite_ref-26" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-26"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>24<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-27" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-27"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>25<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Usborne-2018_10-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Usborne-2018-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>8<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-28" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>26<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk was <a href="/wiki/Baptism" title="Baptism">baptized</a> as a child in the <a href="/wiki/Anglican_Church_of_Southern_Africa" title="Anglican Church of Southern Africa">Anglican Church of Southern Africa</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Higgins2024_29-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Higgins2024-29"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Rees2024_30-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Rees2024-30"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>28<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The Musk family was wealthy during Elon's youth.<sup id="cite_ref-Smith_15-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Smith-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Despite both Elon and Errol previously stating that Errol was a part owner of a Zambian emerald mine,<sup id="cite_ref-Smith_15-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Smith-15"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>13<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in 2023, Errol recounted that the deal he made was to receive "a portion of the emeralds produced at three small mines".<sup id="cite_ref-31" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-31"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>29<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-32" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-32"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>30<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Errol was elected to the Pretoria City Council as a representative of the anti-apartheid <a href="/wiki/Progressive_Party_(South_Africa)" title="Progressive Party (South Africa)">Progressive Party</a> and has said that his children shared their father's dislike of <a href="/wiki/Apartheid" title="Apartheid">apartheid</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Eligon-2022_4-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Eligon-2022-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>After his parents divorced in 1979, Elon, aged around 9, chose to live with his father because he had an <i><a href="/wiki/Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica" title="Encyclopædia Britannica">Encyclopædia Britannica</a></i> set and a computer.<sup id="cite_ref-33" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-33"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>31<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-sjmn20140411_6-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sjmn20140411-6"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>4<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Isaacson_12-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Isaacson-12"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>10<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Elon later regretted his decision and became estranged from his father.<sup id="cite_ref-rollingstone20171115_34-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rollingstone20171115-34"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Elon has recounted trips to a wilderness school that he described as a "paramilitary <i><a href="/wiki/Lord_of_the_Flies" title="Lord of the Flies">Lord of the Flies</a></i>" where "bullying was a virtue" and children were encouraged to fight over rations.<sup id="cite_ref-35" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-35"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>33<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In one incident, after an altercation with a fellow pupil, Elon was thrown down concrete steps and beaten severely, leading to him being hospitalized for his injuries.<sup id="cite_ref-Isaacson23_36-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Isaacson23-36"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Elon described his father berating him after he was discharged from the hospital.<sup id="cite_ref-Isaacson23_36-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Isaacson23-36"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>34<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Errol denied berating Elon and claimed, "The [other] boy had just lost his father to suicide, and Elon had called him stupid. Elon had a tendency to call people stupid. How could I possibly blame that child?"<sup id="cite_ref-Bhaimiya_37-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bhaimiya-37"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>35<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Elon was an enthusiastic reader of books, and had attributed his success in part to having read <i><a href="/wiki/The_Lord_of_the_Rings" title="The Lord of the Rings">The Lord of the Rings</a></i>, the <a href="/wiki/Foundation_(book_series)" class="mw-redirect" title="Foundation (book series)"><i>Foundation</i> series</a>, and <a href="/wiki/The_Hitchhiker%27s_Guide_to_the_Galaxy_(novel)" title="The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (novel)"><i>The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy</i></a>.<sup id="cite_ref-NewYorker2009_14-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NewYorker2009-14"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>12<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-38" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-38"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> At age ten, he developed an interest in computing and video games, teaching himself how to program from the <a href="/wiki/VIC-20" title="VIC-20">VIC-20</a> user manual.<sup id="cite_ref-Vance_39-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vance-39"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>37<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> At age twelve, Elon sold his <a href="/wiki/BASIC" title="BASIC">BASIC</a>-based game <i>Blastar</i> to <i>PC and Office Technology</i> magazine for approximately $500 (equivalent to $1,600 in 2025).<sup id="cite_ref-play_40-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-play-40"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Education">Education</h3></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:PBHS-facade.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="An ornate school building" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PBHS-facade.jpg/250px-PBHS-facade.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="168" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/PBHS-facade.jpg/500px-PBHS-facade.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1146" data-file-height="768"></a><figcaption>Musk graduated from <a href="/wiki/Pretoria_Boys_High_School" title="Pretoria Boys High School">Pretoria Boys High School</a> in South Africa.</figcaption></figure>
<p>Musk attended <a href="/wiki/Waterkloof_House_Preparatory_School" title="Waterkloof House Preparatory School">Waterkloof House Preparatory School</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bryanston_High_School" title="Bryanston High School">Bryanston High School</a>, and then <a href="/wiki/Pretoria_Boys_High_School" title="Pretoria Boys High School">Pretoria Boys High School</a>, where he graduated.<sup id="cite_ref-slate20191204_42-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-slate20191204-42"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk was a decent but unexceptional student, earning a 61/100 in <a href="/wiki/Afrikaans" title="Afrikaans">Afrikaans</a> and a B on his senior math certification.<sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk applied for a Canadian passport <a href="/wiki/Jus_sanguinis" title="Jus sanguinis">through</a> his Canadian-born mother to avoid South Africa's <a href="/wiki/Conscription_in_South_Africa" title="Conscription in South Africa">mandatory military service</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-arrived_44-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-arrived-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> which would have forced him to participate in the apartheid regime,<sup id="cite_ref-Eligon-2022_4-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Eligon-2022-4"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> as well as to ease his path to immigration to the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-Esquire_46-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Esquire-46"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> While waiting for his application to be processed, he attended the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Pretoria" title="University of Pretoria">University of Pretoria</a> for five months.<sup id="cite_ref-47" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-47"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Musk arrived in Canada in June 1989, connected with a second cousin in <a href="/wiki/Saskatchewan" title="Saskatchewan">Saskatchewan</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and worked odd jobs, including at a farm and a lumber mill.<sup id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 1990, he entered <a href="/wiki/Queen%27s_University_at_Kingston" title="Queen's University at Kingston">Queen's University</a> in <a href="/wiki/Kingston,_Ontario" title="Kingston, Ontario">Kingston, Ontario</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Two years later, he transferred to the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania" title="University of Pennsylvania">University of Pennsylvania</a>, where he studied until 1995.<sup id="cite_ref-:6_53-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-53"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Although Musk has said that he earned his degrees in 1995, the University of Pennsylvania did not award them until 1997 – a <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts" title="Bachelor of Arts">Bachelor of Arts</a> in physics and a <a href="/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science" title="Bachelor of Science">Bachelor of Science</a> in economics from the university's <a href="/wiki/Wharton_School" title="Wharton School">Wharton School</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Vance368_54-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vance368-54"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-VanceA1_56-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-VanceA1-56"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-57" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-57"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-58" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-58"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> He reportedly hosted large, ticketed house parties to help pay for tuition, and wrote a business plan for an electronic book-scanning service similar to <a href="/wiki/Google_Books" title="Google Books">Google Books</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-ironman_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ironman-59"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 1994, Musk held two internships in <a href="/wiki/Silicon_Valley" title="Silicon Valley">Silicon Valley</a>: one at energy storage startup Pinnacle Research Institute, which investigated electrolytic <a href="/wiki/Supercapacitor" title="Supercapacitor">supercapacitors</a> for energy storage, and another at <a href="/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California" title="Palo Alto, California">Palo Alto</a>–based startup <a href="/wiki/Rocket_Science_Games" title="Rocket Science Games">Rocket Science Games</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-60" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-60"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-61" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-61"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 1995, he was accepted to a graduate program in <a href="/wiki/Materials_science" title="Materials science">materials science</a> at <a href="/wiki/Stanford_University" title="Stanford University">Stanford University</a>, but did not enroll.<sup id="cite_ref-VanceA1_56-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-VanceA1-56"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Vance368_54-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vance368-54"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Sacchetti1026_62-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sacchetti1026-62"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk decided to join the <a href="/wiki/Dot-com_bubble" title="Dot-com bubble">Internet boom</a> of the 1990s, applying for a job at <a href="/wiki/Netscape" title="Netscape">Netscape</a>, to which he reportedly never received a response.<sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>61<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-arrived_44-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-arrived-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_Washington_Post" title="The Washington Post">The Washington Post</a></i> reported that Musk lacked legal authorization to remain and work in the United States after failing to enroll at Stanford.<sup id="cite_ref-Sacchetti1026_62-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Sacchetti1026-62"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In response, Musk said he was allowed to work at that time and that his student visa transitioned to an <a href="/wiki/H-1B_visa" title="H-1B visa">H1-B</a>. According to numerous former business associates and shareholders, Musk said he was on a student visa at the time.<sup id="cite_ref-64" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-64"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>62<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Business_career">Business career</h2></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Business_career_of_Elon_Musk" title="Business career of Elon Musk">Business career of Elon Musk</a></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Zip2">Zip2</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Zip2" title="Zip2">Zip2</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353403208"><table class="infobox" style="width: 210px; clear: right; float:right;margin:0 0 4px 1.5em"><tbody><tr><th colspan="2" class="infobox-above" style="font-size:115%">External videos</th></tr><tr><td colspan="2" class="infobox-full-data" style="text-align: left"><span class="noviewer" typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="video icon" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png" decoding="async" width="16" height="16" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/40px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="128" data-file-height="128"></a></span> <a rel="nofollow" class="external text" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e7Qh-vwpYH8"><span class="plainlinks">Musk speaks of his early business experience during a 2014 commencement speech at University of Southern California</span></a> on YouTube</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>In 1995, Musk, his brother <a href="/wiki/Kimbal" class="mw-redirect" title="Kimbal">Kimbal</a>, and Greg Kouri founded the web software company <a href="/wiki/Zip2" title="Zip2">Zip2</a> with funding from a group of angel investors.<sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>63<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> They housed the venture at a small rented office in Palo Alto.<sup id="cite_ref-shower_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shower-66"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Replying to <i><a href="/wiki/Rolling_Stone" title="Rolling Stone">Rolling Stone</a></i>, Musk denounced the notion that they started their company with funds borrowed from Elon's father Errol Musk,<sup id="cite_ref-rollingstone20171115_34-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-rollingstone20171115-34"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>32<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> but in a tweet, he recognized that his father contributed 10% of a later funding round.<sup id="cite_ref-twitterzip2_67-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-twitterzip2-67"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company developed and marketed an Internet city guide for the newspaper publishing industry, with maps, directions, and yellow pages.<sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>66<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>According to Musk, "The website was up during the day and I was coding it at night, seven days a week, all the time."<sup id="cite_ref-shower_66-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shower-66"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> To impress investors, Musk built a large plastic structure around a standard computer to create the impression that Zip2 was powered by a small supercomputer.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEVance201764_69-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEVance201764-69"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The Musk brothers obtained contracts with <i><a href="/wiki/The_New_York_Times" title="The New York Times">The New York Times</a></i> and the <i><a href="/wiki/Chicago_Tribune" title="Chicago Tribune">Chicago Tribune</a>,</i><sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>68<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and persuaded the board of directors to abandon plans for a merger with <a href="/wiki/CitySearch" class="mw-redirect" title="CitySearch">CitySearch</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-71" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-71"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk's attempts to become CEO were thwarted by the board.<sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>70<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Compaq" title="Compaq">Compaq</a> acquired Zip2 for $307 million in cash in February 1999 (equivalent to $590,000,000 in 2025),<sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>71<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>72<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and Musk received $22 million (equivalent to $43,000,000 in 2025) for his 7-percent share.<sup id="cite_ref-Vance109_75-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vance109-75"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>73<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="X.com_and_PayPal">X.com and PayPal</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/X.com_(bank)" title="X.com (bank)">X.com (bank)</a>, <a href="/wiki/PayPal" title="PayPal">PayPal</a>, and <a href="/wiki/PayPal_Mafia" title="PayPal Mafia">PayPal Mafia</a></div>
<p>In 1999, Musk co-founded <a href="/wiki/X.com_(bank)" title="X.com (bank)">X.com</a>, an online financial services and e-mail payment company.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>74<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The startup was one of the first <a href="/wiki/Federal_Deposit_Insurance_Corporation" title="Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation">federally insured</a> online banks, and, in its initial months of operation, over 200,000 customers joined the service.<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>75<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company's investors regarded Musk as inexperienced and replaced him with <a href="/wiki/Intuit" title="Intuit">Intuit</a> CEO Bill Harris by the end of the year.<sup id="cite_ref-vance86_78-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vance86-78"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>76<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The following year, X.com merged with online bank <a href="/wiki/Confinity" title="Confinity">Confinity</a> to avoid competition.<sup id="cite_ref-shower_66-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-shower-66"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-vance86_78-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vance86-78"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>76<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Founded by <a href="/wiki/Max_Levchin" title="Max Levchin">Max Levchin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Peter_Thiel" title="Peter Thiel">Peter Thiel</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>78<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Confinity had its own money-transfer service, <a href="/wiki/PayPal" title="PayPal">PayPal</a>, which was more popular than X.com's service.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>79<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Within the merged company, Musk returned as CEO. Musk's preference for <a href="/wiki/Microsoft" title="Microsoft">Microsoft</a> software over <a href="/wiki/Unix" title="Unix">Unix</a> created a rift in the company and caused Thiel to resign.<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>80<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Due to resulting technological issues and lack of a cohesive business model, the board ousted Musk and replaced him with Thiel in 2000.<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>81<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>c<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Under Thiel, the company focused on the PayPal service and was renamed PayPal in 2001.<sup id="cite_ref-vance89_85-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-vance89-85"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>83<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>84<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2002, PayPal was acquired by <a href="/wiki/EBay" title="EBay">eBay</a> for $1.5 billion (equivalent to $2,700,000,000 in 2025) in stock, of which Musk—the largest shareholder with 11.72% of shares—received $175.8 million (equivalent to $320,000,000 in 2025).<sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>85<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>86<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2017, Musk purchased the domain X.com from PayPal for an undisclosed amount, stating that it had sentimental value.<sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>87<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-91"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>88<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="SpaceX">SpaceX</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/SpaceX" title="SpaceX">SpaceX</a></div>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:SpaceX_CEO_Elon_Musk_visits_N%26NC_and_AFSPC_(190416-F-ZZ999-006)_(cropped).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/SpaceX_CEO_Elon_Musk_visits_N%26NC_and_AFSPC_%28190416-F-ZZ999-006%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-SpaceX_CEO_Elon_Musk_visits_N%26NC_and_AFSPC_%28190416-F-ZZ999-006%29_%28cropped%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="364" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/SpaceX_CEO_Elon_Musk_visits_N%26NC_and_AFSPC_%28190416-F-ZZ999-006%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-SpaceX_CEO_Elon_Musk_visits_N%26NC_and_AFSPC_%28190416-F-ZZ999-006%29_%28cropped%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2572" data-file-height="3747"></a><figcaption>Musk explains <a href="/wiki/SpaceX_Starship" title="SpaceX Starship">Starship</a> capabilities to leaders of <a href="/wiki/NORAD" title="NORAD">North American Aerospace Defense Command</a>, U.S. Northern Command, and <a href="/wiki/Space_Operations_Command" class="mw-redirect" title="Space Operations Command">Air Force Space Command</a> in 2019.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2001, Musk became involved with the nonprofit <a href="/wiki/Mars_Society" title="Mars Society">Mars Society</a> and discussed funding plans to place a <a href="/wiki/Space_farming" title="Space farming">growth-chamber for plants</a> on <a href="/wiki/Mars" title="Mars">Mars</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>89<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Seeking a way to launch the greenhouse payloads into space, Musk made two unsuccessful trips to Moscow to purchase <a href="/wiki/Intercontinental_ballistic_missiles" class="mw-redirect" title="Intercontinental ballistic missiles">intercontinental ballistic missiles</a> (ICBMs) from Russian companies <a href="/wiki/NPO_Lavochkin" class="mw-redirect" title="NPO Lavochkin">NPO Lavochkin</a> and <a href="/wiki/Kosmotras" class="mw-redirect" title="Kosmotras">Kosmotras</a>. Musk instead decided to start a company to build affordable rockets.<sup id="cite_ref-Vance-2015_93-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vance-2015-93"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>90<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> With $100 million of his early fortune,<sup id="cite_ref-94" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-94"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>91<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> (equivalent to $180,000,000 in 2025) Musk founded SpaceX in May 2002 and became the company's CEO and Chief Engineer.<sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>92<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-96" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-96"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>93<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>SpaceX attempted its first launch of the <a href="/wiki/Falcon_1" title="Falcon 1">Falcon 1</a> rocket in 2006.<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBerger2021178–182_97-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBerger2021178–182-97"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Although the rocket failed to reach <a href="/wiki/Geocentric_orbit" title="Geocentric orbit">Earth orbit</a>, it was awarded a <a href="/wiki/Commercial_Orbital_Transportation_Services" title="Commercial Orbital Transportation Services">Commercial Orbital Transportation Services</a> program contract from <a href="/wiki/NASA" title="NASA">NASA</a>, then led by <a href="/wiki/Michael_D._Griffin" title="Michael D. Griffin">Mike Griffin</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>95<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>96<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> After two more failed attempts that nearly caused Musk to go bankrupt,<sup id="cite_ref-FOOTNOTEBerger2021178–182_97-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBerger2021178–182-97"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> SpaceX succeeded in launching the Falcon 1 into orbit in 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>97<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Later that year, SpaceX received a $1.6 billion NASA contract (equivalent to $2,400,000,000 in 2025) for <a href="/wiki/Falcon_9" title="Falcon 9">Falcon 9</a>-launched <a href="/wiki/SpaceX_Dragon" title="SpaceX Dragon">Dragon spacecraft</a> flights to the <a href="/wiki/International_Space_Station" title="International Space Station">International Space Station</a> (ISS), replacing the <a href="/wiki/Space_Shuttle" title="Space Shuttle">Space Shuttle</a> after its 2011 <a href="/wiki/Space_Shuttle_retirement" title="Space Shuttle retirement">retirement</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2012, the Dragon vehicle docked <a href="/wiki/SpaceX_COTS_Demo_Flight_2" title="SpaceX COTS Demo Flight 2">with the ISS</a>, a first for a commercial spacecraft.<sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>99<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Working towards its goal of <a href="/wiki/SpaceX_reusable_launch_system_development_program" title="SpaceX reusable launch system development program">reusable rockets</a>, in 2015 SpaceX successfully landed the <a href="/wiki/Multistage_rocket" title="Multistage rocket">first stage</a> of a Falcon 9 on a land platform.<sup id="cite_ref-103" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-103"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>100<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Later landings were achieved on <a href="/wiki/Autonomous_spaceport_drone_ship" title="Autonomous spaceport drone ship">autonomous spaceport drone ships</a>, an ocean-based recovery platform.<sup id="cite_ref-104" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-104"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>101<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2018, SpaceX launched the <a href="/wiki/Falcon_Heavy" title="Falcon Heavy">Falcon Heavy</a>; the <a href="/wiki/Falcon_Heavy_test_flight" title="Falcon Heavy test flight">inaugural mission</a> carried <a href="/wiki/Elon_Musk%27s_Tesla_Roadster" title="Elon Musk's Tesla Roadster">Musk's personal Tesla Roadster</a> as a <a href="/wiki/Boilerplate_(spaceflight)" title="Boilerplate (spaceflight)">dummy payload</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>102<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-106" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-106"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>103<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Since 2019,<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>104<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> SpaceX has been developing <a href="/wiki/SpaceX_Starship" title="SpaceX Starship">Starship</a>, a reusable, <a href="/wiki/Super_heavy-lift_launch_vehicle" title="Super heavy-lift launch vehicle">super heavy-lift launch vehicle</a> intended to replace the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy.<sup id="cite_ref-Roulette-2022_108-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Roulette-2022-108"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>105<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2020, SpaceX launched its first crewed flight, the <a href="/wiki/Crew_Dragon_Demo-2" title="Crew Dragon Demo-2">Demo-2</a>, becoming the first private company to place astronauts into orbit and dock a crewed spacecraft with the ISS.<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>106<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2024, NASA awarded SpaceX an $843 million (equivalent to $865,000,000 in 2025) contract to build a spacecraft that NASA will use to <a href="/wiki/Atmospheric_entry" title="Atmospheric entry">deorbit</a> the ISS at the end of its lifespan.<sup id="cite_ref-110" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-110"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>107<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="Starlink">Starlink</h4></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Starlink" title="Starlink">Starlink</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Starlink_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian War">Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian War</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size mw-halign-left" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Starlink_Mission_(47926144123).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Starlink_Mission_%2847926144123%29.jpg/250px-Starlink_Mission_%2847926144123%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Starlink_Mission_%2847926144123%29.jpg/500px-Starlink_Mission_%2847926144123%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="960" data-file-height="540"></a><figcaption>50 Starlink satellites shortly before deployment to low Earth orbit, 2019</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2015, SpaceX began development of the <a href="/wiki/Starlink" title="Starlink">Starlink</a> constellation of <a href="/wiki/Low_Earth_orbit" title="Low Earth orbit">low Earth orbit</a> satellites to provide <a href="/wiki/Satellite_Internet_access" title="Satellite Internet access">satellite Internet access</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>108<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> After the launch of prototype satellites in 2018, the first large constellation was deployed in May 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-NYT-20190601_112-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NYT-20190601-112"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>109<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> As of May 2025<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" data-mw-original-href="//en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elon_Musk&action=edit" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Elon_Musk&action=edit">[update]</a></sup>, over 7,600 Starlink satellites are operational,<sup id="cite_ref-sn2674441_113-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sn2674441-113"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>110<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> comprising 65% of all operational Earth satellites.<sup id="cite_ref-d933_114-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-d933-114"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>111<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The total cost of the decade-long project to design, build, and deploy the constellation was estimated by SpaceX in 2020 to be $10 billion (equivalent to $12,000,000,000 in 2025).<sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>112<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-118" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-118"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>d<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>During the <a href="/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine" class="mw-redirect" title="Russian invasion of Ukraine">Russian invasion of Ukraine</a>, Musk provided free <a href="/wiki/Starlink_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_War" class="mw-redirect" title="Starlink in the Russo-Ukrainian War">Starlink service to Ukraine</a>, permitting Internet access and communication at a yearly cost to SpaceX of $400 million (equivalent to $440,000,000 in 2025).<sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>115<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-CNN_2022-10-13_120-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNN_2022-10-13-120"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>116<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>117<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>118<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>119<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> However, Musk refused to block <a href="/wiki/Mass_media_in_Russia" title="Mass media in Russia">Russian state media</a> on Starlink.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>120<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-125" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-125"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>121<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2023, Musk denied Ukraine's request to activate Starlink over <a href="/wiki/Crimea" title="Crimea">Crimea</a> to aid an attack against the Russian navy, citing fears of a nuclear response.<sup id="cite_ref-Copp_2023_b431_126-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Copp_2023_b431-126"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>122<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>123<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>124<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Tesla">Tesla</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Tesla,_Inc." title="Tesla, Inc.">Tesla, Inc.</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Elon_Musk,_Tesla_Factory,_Fremont_(CA,_USA)_(8765031426).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Musks stands, arms crossed and grinning, before a Tesla Model S" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Elon_Musk%2C_Tesla_Factory%2C_Fremont_%28CA%2C_USA%29_%288765031426%29.jpg/250px-Elon_Musk%2C_Tesla_Factory%2C_Fremont_%28CA%2C_USA%29_%288765031426%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="208" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Elon_Musk%2C_Tesla_Factory%2C_Fremont_%28CA%2C_USA%29_%288765031426%29.jpg/500px-Elon_Musk%2C_Tesla_Factory%2C_Fremont_%28CA%2C_USA%29_%288765031426%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2224" data-file-height="1848"></a><figcaption>Musk next to a <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Model_S" title="Tesla Model S">Tesla Model S</a>, 2011</figcaption></figure>
<p><a href="/wiki/Tesla,_Inc." title="Tesla, Inc.">Tesla, Inc.</a>, originally Tesla Motors, was incorporated in July 2003 by <a href="/wiki/Martin_Eberhard" title="Martin Eberhard">Martin Eberhard</a> and <a href="/wiki/Marc_Tarpenning" title="Marc Tarpenning">Marc Tarpenning</a>. Both men played active roles in the company's early development prior to Musk's involvement.<sup id="cite_ref-timelinefacts_129-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-timelinefacts-129"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>125<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk led the <a href="/wiki/Series_A_round" title="Series A round">Series A round</a> of investment in February 2004; he invested $6.35 million (equivalent to $11,000,000 in 2025), became the majority shareholder, and joined Tesla's board of directors as chairman.<sup id="cite_ref-130" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-130"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>126<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-131" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-131"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk took an active role within the company and oversaw <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Roadster_(first_generation)" title="Tesla Roadster (first generation)">Roadster</a> product design, but was not deeply involved in day-to-day business operations.<sup id="cite_ref-132" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-132"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Following a series of escalating conflicts in 2007 and the <a href="/wiki/2008_financial_crisis" title="2008 financial crisis">2008 financial crisis</a>, Eberhard was ousted from the firm.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>129<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources" title="Wikipedia:Citing sources"><span title="This citation requires a reference to the specific page or range of pages in which the material appears. (September 2022)">page needed</span></a></i>]</sup><sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>130<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Musk assumed leadership of the company as CEO and product architect in 2008.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>131<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A 2009 lawsuit settlement with Eberhard designated Musk as a Tesla co-founder, along with Tarpenning and two others.<sup id="cite_ref-CNET_136-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNET-136"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>132<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-FastCompany_137-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FastCompany-137"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>133<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Tesla began delivery of the Roadster, an electric sports car, in 2008. With sales of about 2,500 vehicles, it was the first <a href="/wiki/Mass_production" title="Mass production">mass production</a> all-electric car to use <a href="/wiki/Lithium-ion_battery" title="Lithium-ion battery">lithium-ion battery</a> cells.<sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>134<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Under Musk, Tesla has since launched several well-selling electric vehicles, including the four-door sedan <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Model_S" title="Tesla Model S">Model S</a> (2012), the <a href="/wiki/Crossover_(automobile)" class="mw-redirect" title="Crossover (automobile)">crossover</a> <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Model_X" title="Tesla Model X">Model X</a> (2015), the mass-market sedan <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Model_3" title="Tesla Model 3">Model 3</a> (2017), the crossover <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Model_Y" title="Tesla Model Y">Model Y</a> (2020), and the pickup truck <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Cybertruck" title="Tesla Cybertruck">Cybertruck</a> (2023).<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>135<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>137<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>138<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Krisher_2023_143-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Krisher_2023-143"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>139<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company has also constructed multiple lithium-ion battery and electric vehicle factories, called <a href="/wiki/Gigafactory" title="Gigafactory">Gigafactories</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-144" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-144"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>140<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2026, <a href="/wiki/Jon_McNeill" title="Jon McNeill">Jon McNeill</a>, who served as president of Tesla from 2015 to 2018 and oversaw a period of revenue growth from $2 billion to $20 billion, published <i>The Algorithm</i>, a book detailing the five-step operational framework used at Tesla and SpaceX.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2020, Musk resigned as chairman of the board as part of the settlement of a <a href="#Legal_affairs">lawsuit from the SEC</a> over him tweeting that funding had been "secured" for potentially taking Tesla private.<sup id="cite_ref-Goldstein_27-9-18_146-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Goldstein_27-9-18-146"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>142<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:7_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:7-147"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>143<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Since its <a href="/wiki/Initial_public_offering" title="Initial public offering">initial public offering</a> in 2010,<sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Tesla stock has risen significantly; it became the most valuable carmaker in summer 2020,<sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>145<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and it entered the <a href="/wiki/S%26P_500" title="S&P 500">S&P 500</a> later that year.<sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>148<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October 2021, it reached a market capitalization of $1 trillion (equivalent to $1,200,000,000,000 in 2025), the sixth company in U.S. history to do so.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>149<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading4"><h4 id="SolarCity_and_Tesla_Energy">SolarCity and Tesla Energy</h4></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/SolarCity" title="SolarCity">SolarCity</a> and <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Energy" title="Tesla Energy">Tesla Energy</a></div>
<p>Musk provided the initial concept and financial capital for <a href="/wiki/SolarCity" title="SolarCity">SolarCity</a>, which his cousins <a href="/wiki/Lyndon_Rive" title="Lyndon Rive">Lyndon</a> and Peter Rive founded in 2006.<sup id="cite_ref-154" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-154"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>150<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By 2013, SolarCity was the second largest provider of solar power systems in the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-155" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-155"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>151<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2014, Musk promoted the idea of SolarCity building an advanced production facility in <a href="/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York" title="Buffalo, New York">Buffalo</a>, New York, triple the size of the largest solar plant in the United States.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Construction of <a href="/wiki/Gigafactory_New_York" title="Gigafactory New York">the factory</a> started in 2014 and was completed in 2017. It operated as a joint venture with <a href="/wiki/Panasonic" title="Panasonic">Panasonic</a> until early 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Tesla acquired SolarCity for $2 billion in 2016 (equivalent to $2,700,000,000 in 2025) and merged it with its battery unit to create <a href="/wiki/Tesla_Energy" title="Tesla Energy">Tesla Energy</a>. The deal's announcement resulted in a more than 10% drop in Tesla's stock price; at the time, SolarCity was facing liquidity issues.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_159-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-159"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Multiple shareholder groups filed a lawsuit against Musk and Tesla's directors, stating that the purchase of SolarCity was done solely to benefit Musk and came at the expense of Tesla and its shareholders.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Tesla directors settled the lawsuit in January 2020, leaving Musk the sole remaining defendant.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Two years later, the court ruled in Musk's favor.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_159-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-159"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Neuralink">Neuralink</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Neuralink" title="Neuralink">Neuralink</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Elon_Musk_and_the_Neuralink_Future.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Musk standing next to bulky medical equipment on a stage" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Elon_Musk_and_the_Neuralink_Future.jpg/250px-Elon_Musk_and_the_Neuralink_Future.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="163" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Elon_Musk_and_the_Neuralink_Future.jpg/500px-Elon_Musk_and_the_Neuralink_Future.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3780" data-file-height="2460"></a><figcaption>Musk discussing a <a href="/wiki/Neuralink" title="Neuralink">Neuralink</a> device during a live demonstration in 2020</figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2016, Musk co-founded <a href="/wiki/Neuralink" title="Neuralink">Neuralink</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Neurotechnology" title="Neurotechnology">neurotechnology</a> startup, with an investment of $100 million.<sup id="cite_ref-sew_164-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sew-164"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-neuraverge_165-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-neuraverge-165"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Neuralink aims to integrate the human brain with <a href="/wiki/Artificial_intelligence" title="Artificial intelligence">artificial intelligence</a> (AI) by creating devices that are embedded in the brain. Such technology could enhance memory or allow the devices to communicate with software.<sup id="cite_ref-neuraverge_165-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-neuraverge-165"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The company also hopes to develop devices to treat neurological conditions like <a href="/wiki/Spinal_cord_injury" title="Spinal cord injury">spinal cord injuries</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-pig_167-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pig-167"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 2022, Neuralink announced that clinical trials would begin by the end of the year.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In September 2023, the <a href="/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration" title="Food and Drug Administration">Food and Drug Administration</a> approved Neuralink to initiate six-year human trials.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Neuralink has conducted <a href="/wiki/Animal_testing" title="Animal testing">animal testing</a> on <a href="/wiki/Macaque" title="Macaque">macaques</a> at the <a href="/wiki/University_of_California,_Davis" title="University of California, Davis">University of California, Davis</a>. In 2021, the company released a video in which a macaque played the video game <i><a href="/wiki/Pong" title="Pong">Pong</a></i> via a Neuralink implant. The company's animal trials—which have caused the deaths of some monkeys—have led to claims of <a href="/wiki/Cruelty_to_animals" title="Cruelty to animals">animal cruelty</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Physicians_Committee_for_Responsible_Medicine" title="Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine">Physicians Committee for Responsible Medicine</a> has alleged that Neuralink violated the <a href="/wiki/Animal_Welfare_Act_of_1966" title="Animal Welfare Act of 1966">Animal Welfare Act</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Employees have complained that pressure from Musk to accelerate development has led to botched experiments and unnecessary animal deaths. In 2022, a federal probe was launched into possible animal welfare violations by Neuralink.<sup id="cite_ref-botched_monkeys_171-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-botched_monkeys-171"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template" style="white-space:nowrap;">[<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items" title="Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers"><span title="This information is in need of an update. (October 2025)">needs update</span></a></i>]</sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="The_Boring_Company">The Boring Company</h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/The_Boring_Company" title="The Boring Company">The Boring Company</a></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Elon_Musk_Accelerates_the_Boring_(45716125474).jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img alt="Musk speaks to a crowd of journalists. Behind him is a lighted tunnel." src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Elon_Musk_Accelerates_the_Boring_%2845716125474%29.jpg/250px-Elon_Musk_Accelerates_the_Boring_%2845716125474%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="169" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/Elon_Musk_Accelerates_the_Boring_%2845716125474%29.jpg/500px-Elon_Musk_Accelerates_the_Boring_%2845716125474%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5161" data-file-height="3499"></a><figcaption>Musk during the 2018 inauguration of the <a href="/wiki/Boring_test_tunnel" class="mw-redirect" title="Boring test tunnel">Boring test tunnel</a> in <a href="/wiki/Hawthorne,_California" title="Hawthorne, California">Hawthorne, California</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In 2017, Musk founded the Boring Company to construct tunnels; he also revealed plans for specialized, underground, high-occupancy vehicles that could travel up to 150 miles per hour (240 km/h) and thus circumvent above-ground traffic in major cities.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-cnndogecoin_173-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnndogecoin-173"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Early in 2017, the company began discussions with regulatory bodies and initiated construction of a 30-foot (9.1 m) wide, 50-foot (15 m) long, and 15-foot (4.6 m) deep "test trench" on the premises of SpaceX's offices, as that required no permits.<sup id="cite_ref-boring_174-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-boring-174"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Boring_test_tunnel" class="mw-redirect" title="Boring test tunnel">Los Angeles tunnel</a>, less than two miles (3.2 km) in length, debuted to journalists in 2018. It used Tesla Model Xs and was reported to be a rough ride while traveling at suboptimal speeds.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Two tunnel projects announced in 2018, in Chicago and West Los Angeles, have been canceled.<sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> A tunnel beneath the <a href="/wiki/Las_Vegas_Convention_Center" title="Las Vegas Convention Center">Las Vegas Convention Center</a> was completed in early 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Local officials have approved further expansions of the tunnel system.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="X_Corp.">X Corp. <span class="anchor" id="X_corp."></span></h3></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441"><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Acquisition_of_Twitter_by_Elon_Musk" title="Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk">Acquisition of Twitter by Elon Musk</a> and <a href="/wiki/Twitter_under_Elon_Musk" title="Twitter under Elon Musk">Twitter under Elon Musk</a></div>
