</p><p>In a pivotal moment, Sega's president, <a href="/wiki/Shoichiro_Irimajiri" title="Shoichiro Irimajiri">Shoichiro Irimajiri</a>, visited Huang in person to inform him that Sega had decided to choose another vendor for the Dreamcast. However, Irimajiri believed in Nvidia's potential and persuaded Sega's management to invest $5 million into the company. Huang later reflected that this funding was all that kept Nvidia afloat, and that Irimajiri's "understanding and generosity gave us six months to live".<sup id="cite_ref-wsj_cohen_2024_39-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wsj_cohen_2024-39"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 1996, Huang laid off more than half of Nvidia's employees—reducing headcount from 100 to 40—and focused the company's remaining resources on developing a graphics accelerator product optimized for processing triangle primitives: the <a href="/wiki/RIVA_128" title="RIVA 128">RIVA 128</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-7" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Peddie_37-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Peddie-37"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By the time the RIVA 128 was released in August 1997, Nvidia had only enough money left for one month's payroll.<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-8" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The sense of impending failure became so pervasive that it gave rise to Nvidia's unofficial company motto: "Our company is thirty days from going out of business."<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-9" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Huang began internal presentations to Nvidia staff with those words for many years.<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-10" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia sold about a million RIVA 128 units within four months,<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-11" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and used the revenue to fund development of its next generation of products.<sup id="cite_ref-Peddie_37-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Peddie-37"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>36<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In 1998, the release of the <a href="/wiki/RIVA_TNT" title="RIVA TNT">RIVA TNT</a> helped solidify Nvidia's reputation as a leader in graphics technology.<sup id="cite_ref-40" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-40"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>39<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Public_company">Public company</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section: Public company"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Nvidia went public on January 22, 1999.<sup id="cite_ref-41" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-41"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>40<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-42" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-42"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>41<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-43" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-43"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>42<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Investing in Nvidia after it had already failed to deliver on its contract turned out to be Irimajiri's best decision as Sega's president. After Irimajiri left Sega in 2000, Sega sold its Nvidia stock for $15 million.<sup id="cite_ref-wsj_cohen_2024_39-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wsj_cohen_2024-39"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>38<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In late 1999, Nvidia released the <a href="/wiki/GeForce_256" title="GeForce 256">GeForce 256</a> (NV10), its first product expressly marketed as a GPU, which was most notable for introducing onboard <a href="/wiki/Transform,_clipping,_and_lighting" title="Transform, clipping, and lighting">transformation and lighting</a> (T&L) to consumer-level 3D hardware. Running at 120 MHz and featuring four-pixel pipelines, it implemented advanced video acceleration, <a href="/wiki/Motion_compensation" title="Motion compensation">motion compensation</a>, and hardware sub-picture <a href="/wiki/Alpha_compositing" title="Alpha compositing">alpha blending</a>. The GeForce outperformed existing products by a wide margin.
</p><p>Because its products were performing well, Nvidia won the contract to develop the graphics hardware for Microsoft's Xbox game console, which included a $200 million advance. However, the project took many of its best engineers away from other projects. In the short term this did not matter, and the <a href="/wiki/GeForce_2_GTS" class="mw-redirect" title="GeForce 2 GTS">GeForce 2 GTS</a> shipped in the summer of 2000. In December 2000, Nvidia reached an agreement to acquire the intellectual assets of its one-time rival <a href="/wiki/3dfx_Interactive" class="mw-redirect" title="3dfx Interactive">3dfx</a>, a pioneer in consumer 3D graphics technology leading the field from the mid-1990s until 2000.<sup id="cite_ref-44" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-44"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>43<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-45" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-45"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>44<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The acquisition process was finalized in April 2002.<sup id="cite_ref-46" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-46"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>45<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2001, <a href="/wiki/S%26P_Global_Ratings" title="S&P Global Ratings">Standard & Poor's</a> selected Nvidia to replace the departing <a href="/wiki/Enron" title="Enron">Enron</a> in the S&P 500 stock index, meaning that index funds would need to hold Nvidia shares going forward.<sup id="cite_ref-Popina_47-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Popina-47"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In July 2002, Nvidia acquired <a href="/wiki/Exluna" class="mw-redirect" title="Exluna">Exluna</a> for an undisclosed sum. Exluna made software-rendering tools and the personnel were merged into the Cg project.<sup id="cite_ref-48" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-48"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>47<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In August 2003, Nvidia acquired MediaQ for approximately US$70 million.<sup id="cite_ref-49" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-49"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>48<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> It launched <a href="/wiki/GoForce" title="GoForce">GoForce</a> the following year. On April 22, 2004, Nvidia acquired iReady, also a provider of high-performance <a href="/wiki/TCP_offload_engine" title="TCP offload engine">TCP offload engines</a> and <a href="/wiki/ISCSI" title="ISCSI">iSCSI</a> controllers.<sup id="cite_ref-50" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-50"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>49<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In December 2004, it was announced that Nvidia would assist <a href="/wiki/Sony" title="Sony">Sony</a> with the design of the graphics processor (<a href="/wiki/RSX_%27Reality_Synthesizer%27" class="mw-redirect" title="RSX 'Reality Synthesizer'">RSX</a>) for the <a href="/wiki/PlayStation_3" title="PlayStation 3">PlayStation 3</a> game console. On December 14, 2005, Nvidia acquired <a href="/wiki/Acer_Laboratories_Incorporated" class="mw-redirect" title="Acer Laboratories Incorporated">ULI Electronics</a>, which at the time supplied third-party <a href="/wiki/Southbridge_(computing)" title="Southbridge (computing)">southbridge</a> parts for <a href="/wiki/Chipset" title="Chipset">chipsets</a> to <a href="/wiki/ATI_Technologies" title="ATI Technologies">ATI</a>, Nvidia's competitor.<sup id="cite_ref-51" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-51"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>50<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In March 2006, Nvidia acquired <a href="/wiki/Hybrid_Graphics" title="Hybrid Graphics">Hybrid Graphics</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-52" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-52"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>51<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In December 2006, Nvidia, along with its main rival in the graphics industry AMD (which had acquired ATI), received subpoenas from the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Justice" title="United States Department of Justice">United States Department of Justice</a> regarding possible antitrust violations in the graphics card industry.<sup id="cite_ref-53" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-53"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>52<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="2007–2014"><span id="2007.E2.80.932014"></span>2007–2014</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=5" title="Edit section: 2007–2014"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i> named Nvidia its <i>Company of the Year</i> for 2007, citing the accomplishments it made during the said period as well as during the previous five years.<sup id="cite_ref-54" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-54"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>53<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On January 5, 2007, Nvidia announced that it had completed the acquisition of <a href="/wiki/PortalPlayer,_Inc." class="mw-redirect" title="PortalPlayer, Inc.">PortalPlayer, Inc.</a><sup id="cite_ref-55" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-55"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>54<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In February 2008, Nvidia acquired <a href="/wiki/Ageia" title="Ageia">Ageia</a>, developer of <a href="/wiki/PhysX" title="PhysX">PhysX</a>, a <a href="/wiki/Physics_engine" title="Physics engine">physics engine</a> and <a href="/wiki/Physics_processing_unit" title="Physics processing unit">physics processing unit</a>. Nvidia announced that it planned to integrate the PhysX technology into its future <a href="/wiki/Graphics_processing_unit" title="Graphics processing unit">GPU</a> products.<sup id="cite_ref-cnet-nvidiaphysx_56-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-cnet-nvidiaphysx-56"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>55<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-ars-physxsse_57-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ars-physxsse-57"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>56<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In July 2008, Nvidia took a write-down of approximately $200 million on its first-quarter revenue, after reporting that certain mobile chipsets and GPUs produced by the company had "abnormal failure rates" due to manufacturing defects. Nvidia, however, did not reveal the affected products. In September 2008, Nvidia became the subject of a <a href="/wiki/Class_action_lawsuit" class="mw-redirect" title="Class action lawsuit">class action lawsuit</a> over the defects, claiming that the faulty GPUs had been incorporated into certain laptop models manufactured by <a href="/wiki/Apple_Inc." title="Apple Inc.">Apple Inc.</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dell" title="Dell">Dell</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Hewlett-Packard" title="Hewlett-Packard">HP</a>. In September 2010, Nvidia reached a settlement, in which it would reimburse owners of the affected laptops for repairs or, in some cases, replacement.<sup id="cite_ref-pcmag-laptopsettlement_58-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-pcmag-laptopsettlement-58"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>57<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-extremetech-nvidiadefect_59-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-extremetech-nvidiadefect-59"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>58<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On January 10, 2011, Nvidia signed a six-year, $1.5 billion cross-licensing agreement with Intel, ending all litigation between the two companies.<sup id="cite_ref-engadget-nvintel_60-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-engadget-nvintel-60"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>59<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2011, after initially unveiling it at <a href="/wiki/Mobile_World_Congress" class="mw-redirect" title="Mobile World Congress">Mobile World Congress</a>, Nvidia released its <a href="/wiki/ARM_architecture_family" title="ARM architecture family">ARM</a>-based <a href="/wiki/System-on-chip" class="mw-redirect" title="System-on-chip">system on a chip</a> for mobile devices, <a href="/wiki/Tegra_3" class="mw-redirect" title="Tegra 3">Tegra 3</a>. Nvidia claimed that the chip featured the first-ever quad-core mobile CPU.<sup id="cite_ref-tr-tegra3_61-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-tr-tegra3-61"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>60<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-62" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-62"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>61<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2011, it was announced that Nvidia had agreed to acquire <a href="/wiki/Icera" title="Icera">Icera</a>, a baseband chip making company in the UK, for $367 million.<sup id="cite_ref-63" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-63"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>62<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In January 2013, Nvidia unveiled the <a href="/wiki/Tegra_4" class="mw-redirect" title="Tegra 4">Tegra 4</a>, as well as the <a href="/wiki/Shield_Portable" class="mw-redirect" title="Shield Portable">Nvidia Shield</a>, an <a href="/wiki/Android_(operating_system)" title="Android (operating system)">Android</a>-based <a href="/wiki/Handheld_game_console" title="Handheld game console">handheld game console</a> powered by the new system on a chip.<sup id="cite_ref-verge-shieldunveil_64-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-verge-shieldunveil-64"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>63<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On July 29, 2013, Nvidia announced that it acquired <a href="/wiki/The_Portland_Group" title="The Portland Group">PGI</a> from STMicroelectronics.<sup id="cite_ref-65" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-65"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>64<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2013, Nvidia announced its plans to build a new headquarters in the form of two giant triangle-shaped buildings on the other side of San Tomas Expressway (to the west of its existing headquarters complex). The company selected triangles as its design theme. As Huang explained in a blog post, the triangle is "the fundamental building block of computer graphics".<sup id="cite_ref-McMillan_66-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-McMillan-66"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>65<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In 2014, Nvidia <a href="/wiki/Video_game_port" class="mw-redirect" title="Video game port">ported</a> the <a href="/wiki/Valve_Corporation" title="Valve Corporation">Valve</a> games <i><a href="/wiki/Portal_(video_game)" title="Portal (video game)">Portal</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/Half-Life_2" title="Half-Life 2">Half Life 2</a></i> to its <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Shield_Tablet" title="Nvidia Shield Tablet">Nvidia Shield Tablet</a> as Lightspeed Studio.<sup id="cite_ref-67" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-67"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>66<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-68" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-68"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>67<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Since 2014, Nvidia has diversified its business focusing on three markets: gaming, automotive electronics, and mobile devices.<sup id="cite_ref-69" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-69"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>68<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>That same year, Nvidia also prevailed in litigation brought by the trustee of 3dfx's bankruptcy estate to challenge its 2000 acquisition of 3dfx's intellectual assets. On November 6, 2014, in an unpublished memorandum order, the <a href="/wiki/United_States_Court_of_Appeals_for_the_Ninth_Circuit" title="United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit">United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit</a> affirmed the "district court's judgment affirming the bankruptcy court's determination that [Nvidia] did not pay less than fair market value for assets purchased from 3dfx shortly before 3dfx filed for bankruptcy".<sup id="cite_ref-70" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-70"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>69<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="2016–2018"><span id="2016.E2.80.932018"></span>2016–2018</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section: 2016–2018"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>On May 6, 2016, Nvidia unveiled the first GPUs of the <a href="/wiki/GeForce_10_series" title="GeForce 10 series">GeForce 10 series</a>, the GTX 1080 and 1070, based on the company's new <a href="/wiki/Pascal_microarchitecture" class="mw-redirect" title="Pascal microarchitecture">Pascal</a> microarchitecture. Nvidia claimed that both models outperformed its <a href="/wiki/Maxwell_(microarchitecture)" title="Maxwell (microarchitecture)">Maxwell</a>-based Titan X model; the models incorporate GDDR5X and <a href="/wiki/GDDR5" class="mw-redirect" title="GDDR5">GDDR5</a> memory respectively, and use a 16 nm manufacturing process. The architecture also supports a new hardware feature known as simultaneous multi-projection (SMP), which is designed to improve the quality of multi-monitor and <a href="/wiki/Virtual_reality" title="Virtual reality">virtual reality</a> (VR) rendering.<sup id="cite_ref-verge-1080unveil_71-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-verge-1080unveil-71"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>70<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-72" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-72"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>71<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-73" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-73"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>72<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Laptops that include these GPUs and are sufficiently thin – as of late 2017, under 0.8 inches (20 mm) – have been designated as meeting Nvidia's "Max-Q" design standard.<sup id="cite_ref-74" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-74"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>73<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In July 2016, Nvidia agreed to a settlement for a false advertising lawsuit regarding its <a href="/wiki/GTX_970" class="mw-redirect" title="GTX 970">GTX 970</a> model, as the models were unable to use all of their advertised 4 GB of VRAM due to limitations brought by the design of its hardware.<sup id="cite_ref-75" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-75"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>74<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2017, Nvidia announced a partnership with <a href="/wiki/Toyota" title="Toyota">Toyota</a> which would use Nvidia's <a href="/wiki/Drive_PX-series" class="mw-redirect" title="Drive PX-series">Drive PX-series</a> artificial intelligence platform for its autonomous vehicles.<sup id="cite_ref-76" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-76"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>75<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In July 2017, Nvidia and Chinese search giant <a href="/wiki/Baidu" title="Baidu">Baidu</a> announced a far-reaching AI partnership that includes cloud computing, autonomous driving, consumer devices, and Baidu's open-source AI framework PaddlePaddle. Baidu unveiled that Nvidia's Drive PX 2 AI will be the foundation of its autonomous-vehicle platform.<sup id="cite_ref-77" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-77"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>76<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia released the Titan V on December 7, 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-78" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-78"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>77<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-79" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-79"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>78<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia released the Nvidia Quadro GV100 on March 27, 2018.<sup id="cite_ref-80" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-80"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>79<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia released the RTX 2080 GPUs on September 27, 2018. In 2018, <a href="/wiki/Google" title="Google">Google</a> announced that Nvidia's Tesla P4 graphic cards would be integrated into Google Cloud service's artificial intelligence.<sup id="cite_ref-81" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-81"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>80<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2018, on the Nvidia user forum, a thread was started<sup id="cite_ref-82" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-82"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>81<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> asking the company to update users when it would release web drivers for its cards installed on legacy <a href="/wiki/Mac_Pro" title="Mac Pro">Mac Pro</a> machines up to <a href="/wiki/Mac_Pro#1st_generation_(tower)" title="Mac Pro">mid-2012 5,1</a> running the <a href="/wiki/MacOS_Mojave" title="MacOS Mojave">macOS Mojave</a> operating system 10.14. <a href="/wiki/Device_driver" title="Device driver">Web drivers</a> are required to enable graphics acceleration and multiple <a href="/wiki/Computer_monitor" title="Computer monitor">display monitor</a> capabilities of the GPU. On its Mojave update info website, Apple stated that macOS Mojave would run on legacy machines with '<a href="/wiki/Metal_(API)" title="Metal (API)">Metal compatible</a>' graphics cards<sup id="cite_ref-83" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-83"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>82<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and listed Metal compatible GPUs, including some manufactured by Nvidia.<sup id="cite_ref-84" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-84"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>83<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> However, this list did not include Metal compatible cards that currently work in <a href="/wiki/MacOS_High_Sierra" title="MacOS High Sierra">macOS High Sierra</a> using Nvidia-developed web drivers. In September, Nvidia responded, "Apple fully controls drivers for macOS. But if Apple allows, our engineers are ready and eager to help Apple deliver great drivers for macOS 10.14 (Mojave)."<sup id="cite_ref-85" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-85"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>84<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October, Nvidia followed this up with another public announcement, "Apple fully controls drivers for macOS. Unfortunately, Nvidia currently cannot release a driver unless it is approved by Apple,"<sup id="cite_ref-86" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-86"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>85<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> suggesting a possible rift between the two companies.<sup id="cite_ref-87" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-87"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>86<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By January 2019, with still no sign of the enabling web drivers, <a href="/wiki/Apple_community#Online_publishers" title="Apple community">Apple Insider</a> weighed into the controversy with a claim that Apple management "doesn't want Nvidia support in macOS".<sup id="cite_ref-88" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-88"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>87<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The following month, Apple Insider followed this up with another claim that Nvidia support was abandoned because of "relational issues in the past",<sup id="cite_ref-89" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-89"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>88<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and that Apple was developing its own GPU technology.<sup id="cite_ref-90" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-90"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>89<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Without Apple-approved Nvidia web drivers, Apple users are faced with replacing their Nvidia cards with a competing supported brand, such as <a href="/wiki/AMD_Radeon" class="mw-redirect" title="AMD Radeon">AMD Radeon</a> from the list recommended by Apple.<sup id="cite_ref-91" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-91"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>90<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="2019_acquisition_of_Mellanox_Technologies">2019 acquisition of Mellanox Technologies</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section: 2019 acquisition of Mellanox Technologies"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Nvidia_Yokneam_Office.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Nvidia_Yokneam_Office.jpg/250px-Nvidia_Yokneam_Office.jpg" decoding="async" width="250" height="187" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/Nvidia_Yokneam_Office.jpg/500px-Nvidia_Yokneam_Office.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4032" data-file-height="3024"></a><figcaption>Nvidia Yokneam office (former <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox Technologies</a>) in <a href="/wiki/Yokneam_Illit" title="Yokneam Illit">Yokneam Illit</a>, <a href="/wiki/Israel" title="Israel">Israel</a>, in March 2023</figcaption></figure>
<p>On March 11, 2019, Nvidia announced a deal to buy <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox Technologies</a> for $6.9 billion<sup id="cite_ref-92" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-92"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>91<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> to substantially expand its footprint in the high-performance computing market. The acquisition of the Israeli firm, a longtime supplier to the Israeli military, led to the 2023 launch of "Israel-1," described as the country's most powerful AI supercomputer.<sup id="cite_ref-93" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-93"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>92<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2019, Nvidia announced new RTX Studio laptops. The creators say that the new laptop is going to be seven times faster than a top-end MacBook Pro with a <a href="/wiki/Core_i9" class="mw-redirect" title="Core i9">Core i9</a> and AMD's <a href="/wiki/Radeon_Pro_Vega" class="mw-redirect" title="Radeon Pro Vega">Radeon Pro Vega</a> 20 graphics in apps like <a href="/wiki/Autodesk_Maya" title="Autodesk Maya">Maya</a> and RedCine-X Pro.<sup id="cite_ref-94" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-94"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>93<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In August 2019, Nvidia announced <i><a href="/wiki/Minecraft_RTX" class="mw-redirect" title="Minecraft RTX">Minecraft RTX</a></i>, an official Nvidia-developed patch for the game <i><a href="/wiki/Minecraft" title="Minecraft">Minecraft</a></i> adding real-time DXR ray tracing exclusively to the Windows 10 version of the game. The whole game is, in Nvidia's words, "refit" with <a href="/wiki/Path_tracing" title="Path tracing">path tracing</a>, which dramatically affects the way light, reflections, and shadows work inside the engine.<sup id="cite_ref-95" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-95"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>94<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="2020–2023"><span id="2020.E2.80.932023"></span>2020–2023</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section: 2020–2023"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In May 2020, Nvidia announced it was acquiring <a href="/wiki/Cumulus_Networks" title="Cumulus Networks">Cumulus Networks</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-Techcrunch_96-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Techcrunch-96"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>95<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Post acquisition the company was absorbed into Nvidia's networking business unit, along with <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox</a>.
</p><p>In May 2020, Nvidia developed an <a href="/wiki/Open_source" title="Open source">open-source</a> <a href="/wiki/Ventilator" title="Ventilator">ventilator</a> to address the shortage resulting from the global <a href="/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic" title="COVID-19 pandemic">coronavirus pandemic</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-97" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-97"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>96<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On May 14, 2020, Nvidia officially announced its <a href="/wiki/Ampere_(microarchitecture)" title="Ampere (microarchitecture)">Ampere</a> GPU microarchitecture and the Nvidia A100 GPU accelerator.<sup id="cite_ref-98" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-98"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>97<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-99" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-99"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>98<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In July 2020, it was reported that Nvidia was in talks with <a href="/wiki/SoftBank_Group" title="SoftBank Group">SoftBank</a> to buy <a href="/wiki/Arm_(company)" class="mw-redirect" title="Arm (company)">Arm</a>, a UK-based chip designer, for $32 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-100" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-100"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>99<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 1, 2020, Nvidia officially announced the <a href="/wiki/GeForce_30_series" class="mw-redirect" title="GeForce 30 series">GeForce 30 series</a> based on the company's new Ampere microarchitecture.<sup id="cite_ref-101" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-101"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>100<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-102" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-102"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>101<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 13, 2020, Nvidia announced that it would buy Arm from SoftBank Group for $40 billion, subject to the usual scrutiny, with the latter retaining a 10% share of Nvidia.<sup id="cite_ref-Arm_acquired_103-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Arm_acquired-103"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>102<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NVIDIA_bought_104-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NVIDIA_bought-104"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>103<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-105" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-105"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>104<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-NVIDIA_to_Acquire_Arm_106-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NVIDIA_to_Acquire_Arm-106"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>105<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<figure class="mw-default-size" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Neuer_Testbericht_der_RTX_2080_(Ti)_(%E6%9E%81%E5%AE%A2%E6%B9%BEGeekerwan)_15.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Neuer_Testbericht_der_RTX_2080_%28Ti%29_%28%E6%9E%81%E5%AE%A2%E6%B9%BEGeekerwan%29_15.png/250px-Neuer_Testbericht_der_RTX_2080_%28Ti%29_%28%E6%9E%81%E5%AE%A2%E6%B9%BEGeekerwan%29_15.png" decoding="async" width="250" height="141" class="mw-file-element" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/81/Neuer_Testbericht_der_RTX_2080_%28Ti%29_%28%E6%9E%81%E5%AE%A2%E6%B9%BEGeekerwan%29_15.png/500px-Neuer_Testbericht_der_RTX_2080_%28Ti%29_%28%E6%9E%81%E5%AE%A2%E6%B9%BEGeekerwan%29_15.png 2x" data-file-width="1920" data-file-height="1080"></a><figcaption>Nvidia GeForce RTX 2080 Ti, part of the <a href="/wiki/RTX_20_series" class="mw-redirect" title="RTX 20 series">RTX 20 series</a>, which is the first generation of <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_RTX" title="Nvidia RTX">Nvidia RTX</a></figcaption></figure>
<p>In October 2020, Nvidia announced its plan to build the most powerful computer in <a href="/wiki/Cambridge" title="Cambridge">Cambridge</a>, England. The computer, called Cambridge-1, launched in July 2021 with a $100 million investment and will employ AI to support <a href="/wiki/Medical_open_network_for_AI" title="Medical open network for AI">healthcare research</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-107" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-107"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>106<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-108" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-108"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>107<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> According to Jensen Huang, "The Cambridge-1 supercomputer will serve as a hub of innovation for the UK, and further the groundbreaking work being done by the nation's researchers in critical healthcare and drug discovery."<sup id="cite_ref-109" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-109"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>108<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Also in October 2020, along with the release of the <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_RTX" title="Nvidia RTX">Nvidia RTX</a> A6000, Nvidia announced it is retiring its workstation GPU brand Quadro, shifting its product name to Nvidia RTX for future products and the manufacturing to be <a href="/wiki/Ampere_(microarchitecture)" title="Ampere (microarchitecture)">Ampere</a> architecture-based.<sup id="cite_ref-Smith_110-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Smith-110"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>109<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In August 2021, the proposed takeover of Arm was stalled after the UK's <a href="/wiki/Competition_and_Markets_Authority" title="Competition and Markets Authority">Competition and Markets Authority</a> raised "significant competition concerns".<sup id="cite_ref-111" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-111"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>110<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In October 2021, the <a href="/wiki/European_Commission" title="European Commission">European Commission</a> opened a competition investigation into the takeover. The Commission stated that Nvidia's acquisition could restrict competitors' access to Arm's products and provide Nvidia with too much internal information on its competitors due to their deals with Arm. SoftBank (the parent company of Arm) and Nvidia announced in early February 2022 that they "had agreed not to move forward with the transaction 'because of significant regulatory challenges<span style="padding-right:.15em;">'</span>".<sup id="cite_ref-wsj_20220208_112-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-wsj_20220208-112"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>111<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The investigation was set to end on March 15, 2022.<sup id="cite_ref-113" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-113"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>112<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-114" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-114"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>113<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> That same month, Nvidia was reportedly compromised by a cyberattack.<sup id="cite_ref-115" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-115"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>114<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This would have been the largest semiconductor acquisition in history.<sup id="cite_ref-:5_18-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:5-18"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>17<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:6_19-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:6-19"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>18<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In March 2022, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang mentioned that they were open to having Intel manufacture their chips in the future.<sup id="cite_ref-116" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-116"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>115<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This was the first time the company mentioned that it would work together with Intel's upcoming foundry services.
</p><p>In April 2022, it was reported that Nvidia planned to open a new research center in <a href="/wiki/Yerevan,_Armenia" class="mw-redirect" title="Yerevan, Armenia">Yerevan, Armenia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-117" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-117"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>116<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2022, Nvidia opened Voyager, the second of the two giant buildings at its new headquarters complex to the west of the old one. Unlike its smaller and older sibling Endeavor, the triangle theming is used more "sparingly" in Voyager.<sup id="cite_ref-Shankland_118-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Shankland-118"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>117<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-119" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-119"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>118<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2022, Nvidia announced its next-generation automotive-grade chip, <a href="/wiki/Nvidia_Drive#DRIVE_Thor" title="Nvidia Drive">Drive Thor</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-120" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-120"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>119<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-121" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-121"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>120<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2022, Nvidia announced a collaboration with the <a href="/wiki/Broad_Institute_of_MIT_and_Harvard_University" class="mw-redirect" title="Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard University">Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard</a> related to the entire suite of Nvidia's <a href="/wiki/Artificial_intelligence" title="Artificial intelligence">AI</a>-powered healthcare software suite called Clara, that includes <a href="/wiki/NVIDIA_Parabricks" class="mw-redirect" title="NVIDIA Parabricks">Parabricks</a> and <a href="/wiki/Medical_open_network_for_AI" title="Medical open network for AI">MONAI</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-122" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-122"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>121<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Following <a href="/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce" title="United States Department of Commerce">United States Department of Commerce</a> regulations which placed an <a href="/wiki/China%E2%80%93United_States_trade_war#Biden_administration_restrictions" title="China–United States trade war">embargo on exports to China</a> of advanced microchips, which went into effect in October 2022, Nvidia saw its data center chip added to the export control list. The next month, the company unveiled a new advanced chip in China, called the A800 GPU, that met the export control rules.<sup id="cite_ref-123" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-123"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>122<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In September 2023, <a href="/wiki/Getty_Images" title="Getty Images">Getty Images</a> announced that it was partnering with Nvidia to launch Generative AI by Getty Images, a new tool that lets people create images using Getty's library of licensed photos. Getty will use Nvidia's Edify model, which is available on Nvidia's <a href="/wiki/Generative_AI" title="Generative AI">generative AI</a> model library Picasso.<sup id="cite_ref-124" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-124"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>123<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 26, 2023, Denny's CEO <a href="/wiki/Kelli_Valade" title="Kelli Valade">Kelli Valade</a> joined Huang in East San Jose to celebrate the founding of Nvidia at Denny's on Berryessa Road, where a plaque was installed to mark the relevant corner booth as the birthplace of a $1 trillion company.<sup id="cite_ref-Witt_28-12" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Witt-28"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>27<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Takahashi_125-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Takahashi-125"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>124<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By then, Nvidia's <a href="/wiki/Hopper_(microarchitecture)" title="Hopper (microarchitecture)">H100</a> GPUs were in such demand that even other <a href="/wiki/Tech_giant" class="mw-redirect" title="Tech giant">tech giants</a> were beholden to how Nvidia allocated supply. <a href="/wiki/Larry_Ellison" title="Larry Ellison">Larry Ellison</a> of <a href="/wiki/Oracle_Corporation" title="Oracle Corporation">Oracle Corporation</a> said that month that during a dinner with Huang at <a href="/wiki/Nobu" title="Nobu">Nobu</a> in <a href="/wiki/Palo_Alto,_California" title="Palo Alto, California">Palo Alto</a>, he and <a href="/wiki/Elon_Musk" title="Elon Musk">Elon Musk</a> of <a href="/wiki/Tesla,_Inc." title="Tesla, Inc.">Tesla, Inc.</a> and <a href="/wiki/XAI_(company)" class="mw-redirect" title="XAI (company)">xAI</a> "were begging" for H100s, "I guess is the best way to describe it. An hour of sushi and begging".<sup id="cite_ref-fitch20240226_126-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-fitch20240226-126"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>125<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2023, it was reported that Nvidia had quietly begun designing <a href="/wiki/ARM_architecture_family" title="ARM architecture family">ARM-based</a> central processing units (CPUs) for Microsoft's <a href="/wiki/Microsoft_Windows" title="Microsoft Windows">Windows</a> operating system with a target to start selling them in 2025.<sup id="cite_ref-127" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-127"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>126<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="2024–2026"><span id="2024.E2.80.932026"></span>2024–2026</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section: 2024–2026"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>In January 2024, <i><a href="/wiki/Forbes" title="Forbes">Forbes</a></i> reported that Nvidia has increased its lobbying presence in Washington, D.C. as American lawmakers consider proposals to <a href="/wiki/Regulation_of_artificial_intelligence" title="Regulation of artificial intelligence">regulate artificial intelligence</a>. From 2023 to 2024, the company reportedly hired at least four government affairs with professional backgrounds at agencies including the United States Department of State and the Department of the Treasury. It was noted that the $350,000 spent by the company on lobbying in 2023 was small compared to a number of major tech companies in the artificial intelligence space.<sup id="cite_ref-128" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-128"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>127<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2024, <a href="/wiki/Raymond_James_Financial" title="Raymond James Financial">Raymond James Financial</a> analysts estimated that Nvidia was selling the H100 GPU in the price range of $25,000 to $30,000 each, while on <a href="/wiki/EBay" title="EBay">eBay</a>, individual H100s cost over $40,000.<sup id="cite_ref-Vanian_129-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vanian-129"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Several major technology companies were purchasing tens or hundreds of thousands of GPUs for their data centers to run <a href="/wiki/Generative_artificial_intelligence" class="mw-redirect" title="Generative artificial intelligence">generative artificial intelligence</a> projects; simple arithmetic implied that they were committing to billions of dollars in capital expenditures.<sup id="cite_ref-Vanian_129-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Vanian-129"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>128<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In February 2024, it was reported that Nvidia was the "hot employer" in Silicon Valley because it was offering interesting work and good pay at a time when other tech employers were downsizing. Half of Nvidia employees earned over $228,000 in 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-Bindley_130-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bindley-130"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>129<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> By then, Nvidia GPUs had become so valuable that they needed special security while in transit to data centers. <a href="/wiki/Cisco" title="Cisco">Cisco</a> chief information officer Fletcher Previn explained at a CIO summit: "Those GPUs arrive by armored car".<sup id="cite_ref-Bousquette_131-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bousquette-131"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>130<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On March 1, 2024, Nvidia became the third company in the history of the United States to close with a market capitalization in excess of $2 trillion.<sup id="cite_ref-Popina_47-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Popina-47"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia needed only 180 days to get to $2 trillion from $1 trillion, while the first two companies, <a href="/wiki/Apple_Inc." title="Apple Inc.">Apple</a> and Microsoft, each took over 500 days.<sup id="cite_ref-Popina_47-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Popina-47"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>46<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> On March 18, Nvidia announced its new AI chip and microarchitecture <a href="/wiki/Blackwell_(microarchitecture)" title="Blackwell (microarchitecture)">Blackwell</a>, named after mathematician <a href="/wiki/David_Blackwell" title="David Blackwell">David Blackwell</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-132" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-132"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>131<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In April 2024, Reuters reported that China had allegedly acquired banned Nvidia chips and servers from <a href="/wiki/Supermicro" title="Supermicro">Supermicro</a> and Dell via tenders.<sup id="cite_ref-133" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-133"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>132<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In June 2024, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and the Justice Department (DOJ) began antitrust investigations into Nvidia, Microsoft and <a href="/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI">OpenAI</a>, focusing on their influence in the AI industry. The FTC led the investigations into Microsoft and OpenAI, while the DOJ handled Nvidia. The probes centered on the companies' conduct rather than mergers. This development followed an open letter from OpenAI employees expressing concerns about the <a href="/wiki/AI_boom" title="AI boom">rapid AI advancements</a> and lack of oversight.<sup id="cite_ref-134" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-134"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>133<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>The company became the world's most valuable, surpassing Microsoft and Apple, on June 18, 2024, after its market capitalization exceeded $3.3 trillion.<sup id="cite_ref-135" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-135"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>134<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Prakash_136-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Prakash-136"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>135<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In June 2024, <a href="/wiki/Trend_Micro" title="Trend Micro">Trend Micro</a> announced a partnership with Nvidia to develop AI-driven security tools, notably to protect the data centers where AI workloads are processed.<sup id="cite_ref-137" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-137"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>136<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This collaboration integrates Nvidia NIM and Nvidia Morpheus with Trend Vision One and its Sovereign and Private Cloud solutions to improve data privacy, real-time analysis, and rapid threat mitigation.<sup id="cite_ref-138" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-138"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>137<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2024, Nvidia introduced a family of open-source <a href="/wiki/Large_language_model#Multimodality" title="Large language model">multimodal large language models</a> called NVLM 1.0, which features a flagship version with 72 billion parameters, designed to improve text-only performance after multimodal training.<sup id="cite_ref-139" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-139"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>138<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-140" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-140"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>139<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2024, Nvidia reported that it had been collaborating with <a href="/wiki/Raytheon" title="Raytheon">Raytheon</a> (a <a href="/wiki/RTX_Corporation" title="RTX Corporation">RTX Corporation</a> business) to “explore network pipelines that accelerate workloads on GPUs and use GPU acceleration software libraries”.<sup id="cite_ref-141" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-141"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>140<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2024, the company was added to the <a href="/wiki/Dow_Jones_Industrial_Average" title="Dow Jones Industrial Average">Dow Jones Industrial Average</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-142" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-142"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>141<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-143" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-143"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>142<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In November 2024, <a href="/wiki/Morgan_Stanley" title="Morgan Stanley">Morgan Stanley</a> reported that "the entire 2025 production" of all of Nvidia's Blackwell chips was "already sold out".<sup id="cite_ref-Kahn_144-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Kahn-144"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>143<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Also in November 2024, the company bought 1.2 million shares of <a href="/wiki/Nebius_Group" title="Nebius Group">Nebius Group</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-145" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-145"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>144<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia was ranked #3 on Forbes' "Best Places to Work" list in 2024.<sup id="cite_ref-146" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-146"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>145<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>As of January 7, 2025, Nvidia's $3.66 trillion market cap was worth more than double of the combined value of AMD, ARM, Broadcom, and Intel.<sup id="cite_ref-Quiros-Gutierrez_147-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Quiros-Gutierrez-147"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>146<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2025, Nvidia saw the largest one-day loss in market capitalization for a U.S. company in history at $600 billion. This was due to <a href="/wiki/DeepSeek" title="DeepSeek">DeepSeek</a>, a Chinese AI startup that developed an advanced AI model at a lower cost and computing power.<sup id="cite_ref-148" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-148"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>147<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> DeepSeek's AI assistant, using the V3 model, surpassed ChatGPT as the highest-rated free app in the U.S. on <a href="/wiki/Apple_Inc." title="Apple Inc.">Apple</a>'s <a href="/wiki/App_Store_(Apple)" title="App Store (Apple)">App Store</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-149" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-149"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>148<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-150" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-150"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>149<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On April 7, 2025, Nvidia released the Llama-3.1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1 <a href="/wiki/Reasoning_language_model" class="mw-redirect" title="Reasoning language model">reasoning</a> large language model, under the Nvidia Open Model License. It comes in three sizes: Nano, Super and Ultra.<sup id="cite_ref-151" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-151"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>150<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On May 28, 2025, Nvidia's second-quarter revenue forecast fell short of market estimates due to U.S. export restrictions impacting AI chip sales to China, yet the company's stock rose 5% as investors remained optimistic about long-term AI demand.<sup id="cite_ref-152" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-152"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>151<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In July 2025, it was announced that Nvidia had acquired CentML, a Canadian-based AI firm.<sup id="cite_ref-153" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-153"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>152<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On July 10, 2025, Nvidia closed for the first time with a market cap above $4 trillion, after its market cap briefly touched and then retreated from that number during the previous day.<sup id="cite_ref-Randewich_154-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Randewich-154"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia became the first company to reach a market cap of $4 trillion.<sup id="cite_ref-Mickle_10-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Mickle-10"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>9<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> At that point, Nvidia was worth more than the combined value of all publicly traded companies in the United Kingdom.<sup id="cite_ref-Randewich_154-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Randewich-154"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>153<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On July 29, 2025, Nvidia ordered 300,000 H20 AI chips from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) due to strong demand from Chinese tech firms like Tencent and Alibaba.<sup id="cite_ref-Reuters_155-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Reuters-155"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>154<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In August 2025, Nvidia and competitor <a href="/wiki/AMD" title="AMD">Advanced Micro Devices</a> agreed to pay 15% of the revenues from certain chip sales in China as part of an arrangement to obtain export licenses.<sup id="cite_ref-156" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-156"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>155<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> Nvidia will pay only for sales of the H20 chips.<sup id="cite_ref-157" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-157"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>156<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 17, 2025, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said he was “disappointed” after the <a href="/wiki/Cyberspace_Administration_of_China" title="Cyberspace Administration of China">Cyberspace Administration of China</a> (CAC) ordered companies including TikTok parent company <a href="/wiki/ByteDance" title="ByteDance">ByteDance</a> and <a href="/wiki/Alibaba_Group" title="Alibaba Group">Alibaba</a> not to purchase the RTX Pro 6000D, a graphics chip made specifically for the Chinese market. China's internet regulator banned the country's largest technology companies from buying Nvidia's artificial intelligence chips as part of efforts to strengthen the domestic industry and compete with the United States. The CAC instructed companies this week to end both testing and orders of the RTX Pro 6000D, which Nvidia had designed as a tailor-made product for China, according to three people with knowledge of the matter.<sup id="cite_ref-158" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-158"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>157<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-159" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-159"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>158<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 18, 2025, Nvidia announced it would invest $5 billion in <a href="/wiki/Intel" title="Intel">Intel</a>, backing the struggling U.S. chipmaker just weeks after the <a href="/wiki/White_House" title="White House">White House</a> arranged a deal for the federal government to take a major stake in the company. The investment will give Nvidia an immediate holding of about 4% in Intel once new shares are issued to finalize the agreement. Nvidia's move provides Intel with fresh support following years of unsuccessful turnaround efforts and will allow Nvidia to offer its powerful GB300 data center servers based on Blackwell GPUs on Intel's X86 architecture.<sup id="cite_ref-160" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-160"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>159<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On September 22, 2025, Nvidia and <a href="/wiki/OpenAI" title="OpenAI">OpenAI</a> announced a memorandum of understanding for a partnership wherein Nvidia would invest $100 billion into OpenAI, and OpenAI would use Nvidia chips and systems in new data centers. OpenAI will build new AI data centers using Nvidia systems, amounting to at least 10 gigawatts system power, which is the equivalent of energy produced by more than four <a href="/wiki/Hoover_Dam" title="Hoover Dam">Hoover Dams</a>. The deal was meant to be a circular arrangement where OpenAI will pay back Nvidia's investment through the purchase of Nvidia's chips, which is a model common in AI partnerships.<sup id="cite_ref-161" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-161"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>160<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> This "circularity" is estimated at $35 billion in new Nvidia chips bought by OpenAI, for every $10 billion Nvidia invests in OpenAI.<sup id="cite_ref-162" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-162"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>161<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> As of January 2026, negotiations had not progressed beyond early stages, and the two companies were rethinking the partnership's structure. In the months leading up to this, chief executive Jensen Huang privately emphasized to industry associates that the original deal was non-binding and not finalized when announced.<sup id="cite_ref-163" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-163"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>162<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In October 2025, a coalition of Nvidia, nonprofit <a href="/wiki/Electric_Power_Research_Institute" title="Electric Power Research Institute">Electric Power Research Institute</a> and <a href="/wiki/PJM_Interconnection" title="PJM Interconnection">PJM Interconnection</a> announced that the first commercial application of software—developed by startup Emerald AI (in which Nvidia invests), that adjusts the energy draw on a power grid in real time was to be deployed at a new data center under construction in <a href="/wiki/Virginia" title="Virginia">Virginia</a>. Dubbed "Aurora", the facility is expected to set a new flexible power standard.<sup id="cite_ref-164" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-164"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>163<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>A server farm dedicated to autonomous AI was also announced in October 2025, as a collaboration between SDS Schönfeld, a data services firm owned by UC Schönfeld, and <a href="/wiki/VAST_Data" title="VAST Data">VAST Data</a>, an Israeli company specializing in AI storage management that collaborates closely with Nvidia. Reports indicate that approximately $30 billion has been secured for the <a href="/wiki/Bet_Yehoshua" class="mw-redirect" title="Bet Yehoshua">Bet Yehoshua</a> server farm. It is expected to feature "tens of petabytes of data infrastructure powered by VAST, along with thousands of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs and Nvidia network processors."<sup id="cite_ref-165" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-165"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>164<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On October 29, 2025, Nvidia became the first company to reach a market capitalization of $5 trillion.<sup id="cite_ref-166" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-166"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>165<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>Nvidia's stock prices fell by 2% on November 11, 2025, as the SoftBank Group dumped its entire Nvidia portfolio worth $5.8 billion, redirecting the capital towards OpenAI instead.<sup id="cite_ref-167" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-167"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>166<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 1, 2025, Nvidia released Alpamayo-R1, an open source, vision-language-action AI model for self-driving vehicles. This was done so that developers and researchers can understand how these models work and come up with standard ways on how the industry can evaluate how they work.<sup id="cite_ref-168" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-168"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>167<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 15, 2025, Nvidia announced the <a href="/wiki/Nemotron" title="Nemotron">Nemotron</a> 3 family of models consisting of Nano, Super and Ultra models, built on a hybrid mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture. Nvidia said Nano has around 30 billion parameters, Super 100 billion, and Ultra 500 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-169" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-169"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>168<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On December 18, 2025, Nvidia announced plans to build a major new research and development campus in Kiryat Tivon, Israel, projected to employ more than 10,000 people and become one of the company's largest sites outside the United States. The 22-acre complex is scheduled to begin construction in 2027, with initial operations expected in 2031, and will include laboratories, green areas, and public facilities. The project reinforces Israel's role as Nvidia's principal international development hub in advanced AI and computing technologies.<sup id="cite_ref-170" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-170"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>169<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2025, it was announced that Nvidia had acquired <a href="/wiki/SchedMD" title="SchedMD">SchedMD</a>, the company behind the open-source workload manager <a href="/wiki/Slurm_Workload_Manager" title="Slurm Workload Manager">Slurm</a>, as part of an effort to expand its AI and high-performance computing software capabilities. Nvidia stated that Slurm would remain open-source and vendor-neutral after the acquisition, with no financial terms disclosed.<sup id="cite_ref-171" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-171"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>170<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In December 2025, <a href="/wiki/CNBC" title="CNBC">CNBC</a> reported Nvidia had agreed to buy assets from <a href="/wiki/Groq" title="Groq">Groq</a> for $20 billion in cash. The deal included a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia for Groq's inference technology. Several of Groq's senior leaders, including its CEO, also agreed to join Nvidia as part of the deal. While both companies said Groq would continue to operate as an individual company, the transaction drew criticism from several industry analysts as a tactic to avoid regulatory scrutiny.<sup id="cite_ref-172" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-172"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>171<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-173" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-173"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>172<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In late 2025, Nvidia entered advanced negotiations to acquire <a href="/wiki/AI21_Labs" title="AI21 Labs">AI21 Labs</a>, an Israeli developer of large language models,<sup id="cite_ref-174" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-174"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>173<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> in a deal valued at as much as $2 billion to $3 billion.<sup id="cite_ref-175" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-175"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>174<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-176" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-176"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>175<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> The proposed transaction is widely described as a talent-focused "acquihire" aimed at integrating AI21's workforce of approximately 200 specialists into Nvidia's global artificial intelligence operations.<sup id="cite_ref-177" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-177"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>176<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> If completed, the transaction would be Nvidia's second-largest Israeli acquisition after its $7 billion purchase of <a href="/wiki/Mellanox_Technologies" title="Mellanox Technologies">Mellanox</a> in 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-178" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-178"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>177<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>At <a href="/wiki/Consumer_Electronics_Show" title="Consumer Electronics Show">CES</a> 2026, CEO Jensen Huang unveiled Nvidia's Vera Rubin AI platform and the Alpamayo open-source model.<sup id="cite_ref-179" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-179"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>178<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Hesai_Technology" title="Hesai Technology">Hesai</a> was also picked as Nvidia's laser technology partner, supplying Lidar sensors to the company, streamlining software, hardware, and data in its autonomous driving products.<sup id="cite_ref-180" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-180"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>179<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In January 2026, Nvidia launched a new weather forecasting service called Earth-2. It is an open-sourced platform that can be incorporated to improve the AI function across models used by scientists, businesses and local governments.<sup id="cite_ref-181" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-181"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>180<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On February 24, 2026, Nvidia announced its acquisition of Israeli startup Illumex, a developer of generative semantic data infrastructure, in a deal reportedly valued at around $60 million.<sup id="cite_ref-182" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-182"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>181<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>On 11 March 2026, Nvidia announced that it will invest $2 billion in artificial intelligence cloud company <a href="/wiki/Nebius_Group" title="Nebius Group">Nebius</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-183" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-183"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>182<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In April 2026, Nvidia announced the release of a new group of open-source artificial intelligence models designed specifically for quantum computing. The development caused a noticeable market surge for allied quantum computing companies.<sup id="cite_ref-184" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-184"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>183<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> During the same month, Nvidia's market momentum was further bolstered by its primary manufacturing partner, TSMC, which reported a 35.1% year-on-year revenue increase for the first quarter of 2026, largely driven by robust global demand for AI accelerators.<sup id="cite_ref-185" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-185"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>184<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>At the GTC conference in March 2026, Nvidia announced the "Vera Rubin" platform, the successor to its Blackwell architecture. The platform includes the Rubin GPU and Vera CPU, designed to scale "agentic AI" and offering significant performance improvements in large-scale AI factories.<sup id="cite_ref-NVIDIA_VeraRubin_186-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NVIDIA_VeraRubin-186"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>185<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>In May 2026, Nvidia announced that it would be partnering with <a href="/wiki/Corning_Inc." title="Corning Inc.">Corning</a> and investing up to 3.2 billion to build 3 new advanced manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas as part of a optical fiber deal.<sup id="cite_ref-187" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-187"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>186<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>

<p>For the fiscal year 2020, Nvidia reported earnings of US$2.796 billion, with an annual revenue of US$10.918 billion, a decline of 6.8% over the previous fiscal cycle. Nvidia's shares traded at over $531 per share, and its market capitalization was valued at over US$328.7 billion in January 2021.<sup id="cite_ref-193" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-193"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>192<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:0_194-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:0-194"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>193<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p>For the Q2 of 2020, Nvidia reported sales of $3.87 billion, which was a 50% rise from the same period in 2019. The surge in sales was driven by people's higher demand for computer technology. According to the financial chief of the company, Colette Kress, the effects of the pandemic will "likely reflect this evolution in enterprise workforce trends with a greater focus on technologies, such as Nvidia laptops and virtual workstations, that enable remote work and virtual collaboration."<sup id="cite_ref-195" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-195"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>194<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> In May 2023, Nvidia crossed $1 trillion in market valuation during trading hours,<sup id="cite_ref-CNBC_5-30-2023_196-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-CNBC_5-30-2023-196"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>195<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup> and grew to $1.2 trillion by the following November.<sup id="cite_ref-197" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-197"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>196<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Ownership">Ownership</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/index.php?title=Nvidia&action=edit&section=14" title="Edit section: Ownership"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>The 10 largest shareholders of Nvidia in early 2026 were:<sup id="cite_ref-sws-ownership_198-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-sws-ownership-198"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>197<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
